shots.voiceover: Let's build a small Koo-joe script in OpenCode. It reads check results from a JSON file, counts passes and failures, and lists the failed checks. We'll follow the code through inspection, execution, tests, and review.
shots.audio: Unchanged Brian ElevenLabs v4 narration; short reading pause after speech
shots.motion: Static readable terminal; crop/punch-in only to actual UI detail

shots.visual: Real Understand Scout map and Scent dry-run selection; do not imply fixture content was inspected
shots.voiceover: We start with the Understand specialist. Scout maps the project, and Scent previews which files would fit a context pack. These results describe the project and file selection. They do not establish the contents of our input fixture. That distinction matters when we decide what the agent actually knows.
shots.audio: Unchanged Brian ElevenLabs v4 narration; short reading pause after speech
shots.motion: Static readable terminal; crop/punch-in only to actual UI detail

shots.visual: Actual ordinary OpenCode Build editing main.kujo, summary.kujo and tests
shots.voiceover: Now we switch to OpenCode's regular Build agent to write the custom code. It separates the summary logic from the command-line entry point and adds tests. The input has four checks. Three pass; docs fails. We want those totals and the failed name in a short, predictable report. This editing step uses OpenCode's normal tools.
shots.audio: Unchanged Brian ElevenLabs v4 narration; short reading pause after speech
shots.motion: Static readable terminal; crop/punch-in only to actual UI detail

shots.visual: Kujo Build source diagnostics and formatting preview
shots.voiceover: Koo-joe Build takes over for verification. Source inspection passes for the entry point and its helper. The formatting preview proposes no changes. These are source checks. We still need to run the program and compare its output with the input.
shots.audio: Unchanged Brian ElevenLabs v4 narration; short reading pause after speech
shots.motion: Static readable terminal; crop/punch-in only to actual UI detail

shots.voiceover: The run preview includes both source files and the JSON input. We review the exact files, command, and effects before approving execution. The program then runs from that reviewed snapshot. The result matches: four checks, three passed, one failed, and docs named below. The snapshot records what ran; it is not an operating-system sandbox.
shots.audio: Unchanged Brian ElevenLabs v4 narration; short reading pause after speech
shots.motion: Static readable terminal; crop/punch-in only to actual UI detail

shots.visual: Actual test preview, approval and test output
shots.voiceover: Next, we preview and approve the interpreter tests, including their expected output. All five fixtures pass, with no expected-output updates. They cover mixed results, all-pass and empty inputs, plus malformed and invalid data through the summary helper. That gives us useful evidence, while leaving one gap for review.
shots.audio: Unchanged Brian ElevenLabs v4 narration; short reading pause after speech
shots.motion: Static readable terminal; crop/punch-in only to actual UI detail

shots.visual: Disclose operator git add -N preparation; real PatchBrief/ChangeBucket output and open CLI coverage finding
shots.voiceover: Before review, I mark the new files for Git's diff view outside OpenCode. PatchBrief summarizes the change; ChangeBucket counts twelve files, one hundred twenty-four additions, and two deletions. The reviewer spots the gap: helper tests cover bad input, but no command-line test proves the error message and nonzero exit code. We keep that finding open.
shots.audio: Unchanged Brian ElevenLabs v4 narration; short reading pause after speech
shots.motion: Static readable terminal; crop/punch-in only to actual UI detail

shots.visual: Real receipt tool result; close with visible remaining CLI error/exit-code test gap
shots.voiceover: Finally, we inspect the receipts for the successful run and tests. They retain the results and artifact locations.
